newsitem.title: CHINA: Tientsin Marine sees 1996 net up.
newsitem.headline: Tientsin Marine sees 1996 net up.

text.p: Tientsin Marine Shipping Co Ltd expects net profits of 90 million yuan for 1996, up from 69.89 million yuan in 1995, based on the expansion of its core shipping business, a company official said on Tuesday.
The figures have yet to be audited, said the official.
The company's shipping business, a key industry supported by the government, had developed greatly in 1996, helped by proceeds from its April B share issue, the official said.
But he added the company's costs had also increased in line with rises in fuel prices. He declined to give further details.
The company posted net profits of 51.14 million yuan for the first half of 1996, up from 24.35 million in first-half 1995.
The official said 1996 earning per share would fall due to the expansion of its share capitalisation but did not elaborate.
In its interim report, the company posted earnings per share of 0.219 yuan for the first half of 1996. The figure for the full year in 1995 was 0.489 yuan.
The company has 233 million shares outstanding, up from 143 million at the end of 1995, following the issue of 90 million B shares in April 1996.
It also listed 34.64 million staff A shares issued in 1992 on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in September 1996.
